recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Do not revert ServiceRequest.intent to the older strict sentence because FHIR-47465 intentionally refined it; any broader harmonization of all request-resource intent comments should be handled as a separate request-pattern issue.
issue_request: FHIR-20604 was an Applied/Persuasive OO change request for R5 asking that intent be highlighted as immutable for request workflow implementers; the resolution specifically requested an updated DeviceRequest.intent comment, and metadata also named ServiceRequest, SupplyRequest, and Task.
initial_application: Two Jira-tagged commits applied the seed in 2024: 2e1351283869728a26929778671dad4bb8c64780 added an immutable comment to DeviceRequest.intent, and 15f50a71de0796cd0db5d1c732b05f221ed7d82c added equivalent wording to ServiceRequest.intent and SupplyRequest.intent. Task.intent already contained immutable guidance in the current source lineage.
additional_context: FHIR-20603 is the parent request-pattern issue that asked for individual immutable-intent trackers and harmonized Request.intent guidance. The current Request pattern says intent is expected to be immutable, with a granularity exception. Later Applied issue FHIR-47465 deliberately changed ServiceRequest.intent to that Request-pattern style, including the granularity exception and the instruction to create a new ServiceRequest basedOn the prior instance when a proposal becomes a plan or order. FHIR-25500, mentioned in a FHIR-20604 comment, addressed publisher '+' display for truncated code-list short names, not the immutability rule. SupplyRequest is no longer active in core fhir.ini and the workflow page links to the OO incubator SupplyRequest.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No source edit was made because DeviceRequest.intent, ServiceRequest.intent, and Task.intent already carry the relevant immutable guidance in active core source; SupplyRequest is outside the active core build and its retained source also already contains the applied immutable wording.
